paragraphs.title: The Siege, the Breach, and Zedekiah’s Escape

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem and besieged it.
The KJV says that the city was broken up in the fourth month of the eleventh year.
easy.q: What happened to the city in the eleventh year of Zedekiah?

answers: By the way of the plain
easy.explanation: They went out of the city by night and went out by the way of the plain.
easy.q: Where did Zedekiah and his men flee?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the breaking through of Jerusalem’s defenses.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the city was broken up” mean?

answers: They were trying to escape secretly
They were going to welcome the Babylonian princes
They were going to the king’s house
medium.explanation: After the Babylonian princes entered the city, Zedekiah and his men fled by night.
medium.q: Why did Zedekiah and the men of war leave the city by night?

answers: He was overtaken in the plains of Jericho
medium.explanation: The Chaldeans pursued him and overtook him in the plains of Jericho.
medium.q: What happened after Zedekiah fled Jerusalem?

answers: The city was prosperous and secure
The city was besieged, breached, and abandoned by its fleeing king
The city was isolated and unaware of the war
challenge.explanation: The siege, the breach, and the king’s flight show the collapse of Jerusalem’s defenses.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of events show about Jerusalem’s condition?

answers: He went to the middle gate
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that Zedekiah and his men went forth from the city by night.
challenge.q: Which detail most clearly shows that Zedekiah’s escape was made secretly?

answers: Zedekiah appointed him as a prince
Zedekiah was brought before him for judgment
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah was captured, brought to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, and judged by him.
challenge.q: What was the result of Zedekiah’s encounter with Nebuchadnezzar?

paragraphs.title: Zedekiah’s Punishment and the Destruction of Jerusalem

answers: He slew them before Zedekiah’s eyes
easy.explanation: The king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes.
easy.q: What did the king of Babylon do to Zedekiah’s sons?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “he put out Zedekiah’s eyes.”
easy.q: What did the king of Babylon do to Zedekiah’s eyes?

easy.explanation: The Chaldeans burned the king’s house and the houses of the people with fire.
easy.q: What did the Chaldeans do to the king’s house and the houses of the people?

medium.explanation: The remnant of the people was taken away to Babylon as captives.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “carried away captive” mean?

answers: The rest were carried away, while the poor were left in the land
Everyone remained in the land and received houses
The poor were carried away, while the rest received vineyards
medium.explanation: Nebuzaradan carried many away captive but left the poor in Judah and gave them vineyards and fields.
medium.q: How did the fate of the poor differ from the fate of the rest of the people?

answers: They were given to the people
medium.explanation: The Chaldeans burned the houses and broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
medium.q: What happened to the walls of Jerusalem?

answers: He was taken from Babylon to Judah
He was taken away as a captive from Jerusalem to Babylon
challenge.explanation: After his eyes were put out and he was bound with chains, he was carried to Babylon.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that Zedekiah was blinded and then taken to Babylon?

answers: The walls were broken, the city was rebuilt, and the people returned
The people were carried away, the city was strengthened, and the walls were repaired
The houses were burned, the walls were broken down, and many people were carried away
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the burning of the houses, the breaking down of the walls, and the captivity of the people.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes the destruction of Jerusalem?

answers: Some were carried away, while the poor remained and received land to work
Only the poor were carried away
challenge.explanation: The poor who had nothing were left in Judah and were given vineyards and fields.
challenge.q: What does leaving the poor in the land show about the distribution of people after the destruction?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar command to protect?

answers: In the court of the prison
easy.explanation: Jeremiah was taken out of the court of the prison.
easy.q: Where was Jeremiah when he was taken out?

easy.explanation: Jeremiah was committed unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.

medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar ordered that Jeremiah be treated well and not harmed.
medium.q: What did the command “do him no harm” mean?

answers: He was taken from the prison court, committed to Gedaliah, and remained among the people
He was taken to Babylon, released, and returned to Jerusalem
He was committed to Zedekiah, carried away, and left in Riblah
medium.explanation: The passage says that Jeremiah was taken from the prison court, committed to Gedaliah, and then dwelt among the people.
medium.q: What was the order of events concerning Jeremiah?

answers: Treat Jeremiah according to his requests and welfare
medium.explanation: The command gave instructions to deal with Jeremiah as he directed.
medium.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar mean by “do unto him even as he shall say unto thee”?

answers: Zedekiah was captured and punished, while Jeremiah was protected and released
Both men were carried away in the same manner
Jeremiah was punished, while Zedekiah was released
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah was judged and carried away, but Jeremiah was ordered to be protected and unharmed.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between Zedekiah’s fate and Jeremiah’s fate?

answers: He was taken out of the land
He was released and lived among the people
challenge.explanation: After being taken from the prison court, Jeremiah was allowed to remain among the people.
challenge.q: What does the statement that Jeremiah “dwelt among the people” mean?

answers: Jeremiah was specifically commanded to be spared from harm
Jeremiah was immediately carried away captive
challenge.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar commanded that Jeremiah be watched over and not harmed.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king of Babylon ordered Jeremiah’s protection?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Rescue to Ebed-melech

easy.explanation: Jeremiah was told to speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian.
easy.q: To whom was Jeremiah told to speak the word of the Lord?

answers: The Lord’s words would come upon it for evil, and not for good
easy.explanation: The Lord said that His words would come upon the city for evil, and not for good.
easy.q: What would happen to Jerusalem according to the word of the Lord?

answers: Because he fled from the city
Because he put his trust in the Lord
Because he was a prince of Babylon
easy.explanation: The Lord connected Ebed-melech’s deliverance with the fact that he had put his trust in Him.

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Ebed-melech would keep his life and escape death.
medium.q: What does the phrase “thy life shall be for a prey unto thee” mean?

answers: The city would suffer, but Ebed-melech would be delivered
The city would be delivered, but Ebed-melech would suffer
Both the city and Ebed-melech would be delivered
medium.explanation: The city would experience calamity, while Ebed-melech would be rescued.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the city and Ebed-melech?

answers: That he would not be given into the hand of the men he feared
That he would receive the king’s house
medium.explanation: The Lord promised that Ebed-melech would not be delivered into the hands of those he feared.
medium.q: What did the Lord promise Ebed-melech “in that day”?

answers: Ebed-melech trusted in the Lord, and therefore he was promised deliverance
Ebed-melech fled, and therefore he became king
Ebed-melech harmed the city, and therefore he was punished
challenge.explanation: The Lord’s promise of deliverance is explained by Ebed-melech’s trust in Him.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears at the end of the passage?

answers: General judgment on the city does not prevent personal deliverance
The city would not suffer at all
Ebed-melech would suffer more than the city
challenge.explanation: Although calamity would come upon Jerusalem, Ebed-melech was promised personal rescue.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between “for evil, and not for good” and Ebed-melech’s rescue emphasize?

challenge.explanation: The word “surely” strongly emphasizes the certainty of the Lord’s promise to deliver him.
challenge.q: Which wording most strongly emphasizes that Ebed-melech would certainly be rescued?
